exposure: intravenous ketamine 0.25 mg/kg following spinal anesthesia
cohort: 60 parturients who underwent elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
finding: Low dose intravenous ketamine before skin incision extended postoperative first analgesia request time by an average of 45.5 min and decreased total analgesia consumption in 24 h.
mod_finding: This study investigated the effect of low-dose intravenous ketamine on postoperative pain after cesarean section, not the impact of different modes of delivery.
